name: John Evelyn Barlas
bio: Scottish poet and revolutionary Socialist, friend of William Morris, author of eight volumes of verse. On Bloody Sunday, 13 November 1887, he was arrested in the Trafalgar Square riot and took a policeman's truncheon to the head, a blow the editors of Wilde's letters say affected his reason. On 31 December 1891 he fired a revolver outside the Speaker's House at Westminster, saying 'I am an anarchist. What I have done is to show my contempt for the House of Commons.' Wilde guaranteed half his £200 bail. He died in a lunatic asylum.
